entries.name: Tahan K. Jones

expected.charges: Desertion / missing movement — refusal to deploy in the 1991 Gulf War as conscientious objector

updates.sentence: Jones reported seven months actually spent in the brig in his first-person candidate statement in the June 6, 2006 Green Party of Alameda County voter guide (p. 10). entries.name: Michele Naar-Obed

expected.charges: Trespass / destruction of government property (Plowshares direct action)
expected.sentence: On August 6, 1995 (Hiroshima Day), as part of the Jubilee Plowshares/East action, Naar-Obed and partners entered Newport News Shipbuilding and boarded the USS Greenville in dry dock, pouring blood and hammering areas associated with cruise-missile capability. Arrested and prosecuted; received 12 months in federal prison. Her probation was later revoked and she was returned to federal custody in July 1999.

updates.sentence: On August 6, 1995 (Hiroshima Day), as part of the Jubilee Plowshares/East action, Naar-Obed and partners entered Newport News Shipbuilding and boarded the USS Greenville in dry dock, pouring blood and hammering areas associated with cruise-missile capability. Arrested and prosecuted; received an 18-month federal prison sentence. The later one-year term for revocation of supervision is a separate episode, not the original sentence. Her probation was later revoked and she was returned to federal custody in July 1999.

sources: Arthur J. Laffin, The Plowshares Disarmament Chronology, 1980-2003, printed page 58 (user-supplied PDF page 70).
entries.rationale: The original sentence was eighteen months; keep it separate from the later one-year revocation term. Neither nominal term is stored as actual time served. All dates and other narrative preserved.
